caption: The drawing depicts a single, cylindrical stoneware crock with a wide open mouth and two small handles, one on each side. The crock is predominantly gray with shading to suggest its rounded form and depth. At the upper center, the word “JORDAN” and the number “1” are inscribed in blue. Below these inscriptions, there is an ornamental blue floral or leaf motif painted directly on the body of the crock. The interior of the crock is shown as dark brown, indicating depth and shadow. The background of the image is plain and light, with no additional objects or details, focusing attention solely on the crock itself. The artist’s signature, “John Tarrantino,” appears in small letters toward the lower left of the drawing.
title: Crock
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
